about: What the content standard (standard/standard.json, prism/content-standard/1 from afflom/prism-devrel) needs to know about the Prism onboarding course: where its pages are, one persona per stakeholder of app/src/Architecture.lex.tex (the Prism-DevRel stakeholders, copied unchanged), which persona guides which page, and the terms the course adds to the shared glossary.

personas.name: Kai
personas.need: A working Prism app of my own, and to know what it proves.

asks.discover: What is Prism, and what would it do for my code?
asks.evaluate: Can I trust what a Prism app claims?
asks.learn: Show me each command and what it prints.
asks.build: How do I make an app that does what I need?
asks.scale: How do I ship it and keep it verified?

personas.name: Iris
personas.need: To pick the right pattern and write a prompt that proves.

asks.discover: How is a Prism app laid out?
asks.evaluate: Which claims are proved, and which are tested?
asks.learn: Walk me through a prompt, one member at a time.
asks.build: Which pattern fits the app I have in mind?
asks.scale: How do I ship it and keep it verified?

personas.name: Vera
personas.need: Evidence that what an app claims is true before it runs.

asks.discover: What does this app claim, and who checks it?
asks.evaluate: What is signed, what is proved, and what does my policy accept?
asks.learn: Where does each check come from?
asks.build: Can a mistake here slip past the checks?
asks.scale: Is the release signed, and can I trace it?

personas.name: Wren
personas.need: To know who each page is for and what it teaches.

asks.discover: Who is each page for, and what do they need first?
asks.evaluate: Which claims can I make, and which are proved?
asks.learn: What does a new user need to try first?
asks.scale: How do the docs stay in step without hand edits?

personas.name: Otto
personas.need: Everything kept in step when the app changes, with no generated file edited by hand.

asks.discover: What runs where, and who owns it?
asks.build: Which command do I need right now?
asks.scale: How do I ship a change without breaking the gate?

reading.tutorial: A tutorial: follow the steps in order. Each one works if the one before it did.
reading.howToGuide: A how-to guide: each section is one step toward one task. Skip what you already have.
reading.reference: Reference: look up what you need. Nothing here asks to be read in order.
reading.explanation: Explanation: read it end to end, away from the keyboard.
reading.home: Start here. Take the modules in order; each ends with a short quiz.

terms.plain: One JSON document (prism/prompt/1) that describes an app. The builder turns it into every facet of a Prism model.
The app member of a prompt (prism/spec/1): purpose, fields, outcomes, rules, properties, examples and limits.
What the app must never or always answer. Each one becomes a theorem the Lean kernel proves for every request.
The BLAKE3 digest that names an app file. Loading recomputes it, and a mismatch refuses the file.
How much signed evidence an app carries: P0 none, P1 a build record, P2 also a proof, P3 also a replay.
The rule for which evidence level is enough to run an app. The default asks for P2.
A table of rules, as in OMG DMN 1.5: each row says which inputs lead to which outcome. The first match decides.
OASIS eXtensible Access Control Markup Language 3.0: a policy decides permit, deny, not applicable or indeterminate.
A model of something that is always in one state and moves between states on events, as in UML 2.5.1.
